subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 3: can a reactiveValues be destroyed, and what's it made of)

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 3: can a reactiveValues be destroyed, and what's it made of)
parts:
Motivation:

Let's say you've been storing the results of an analysis in a reactiveValues object (named revals). Now the user uploads a new data file, and you want to start from a clean slate. However, from the testing I've done it looks like the following...

observe(if(input$fileupload){ revals <- reactiveValues(); ... })

...only creates a reactiveValues() object within the scope of that expression and it is not accessible from any other reactive context. If I save the shinyServer environment and overwrite revals there...

myenv <- environment();
observe(if(input$fileupload){ myenv$revals <- reactiveValues(); ... })

...that does overwrite the "real" revals but observers with a dependency on revals no longer have access to it from that point on and stop invalidating.

So, what is the proper way to reinitialize a reactiveValues object?

I know that I can iterate over the names of revals and individually NULL them, but that's not a clean solution: there will be named NULL objects left inside of revals, I can't predict what invalidations will get triggered and in what order between the first and the last item to be NULL-ed, and for all I know there might be some other data lingering that exists outside the named objects.

Which brings me to my other question: where does a reactiveValues object reside, and what base R class does it inherit from? Environment? List? Function? Is there perhaps some recommended further documentation to read next after having read the "Understanding Reactivity" section of the Shiny tutorial?

Thanks.

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 3: can a reactiveValues be destroyed, and what's it made of)
parts:
I found a hacky way to this:

  1. Make a variable called dummy as an element in the list.
  2. Make your output react to reval$dummy
  3. Just before you re-intialize your list assign dummy to another random.number
  4. Just use <<- to re-assign your reval
<script src="https://gist.github.com/xiaodaigh/6946423.js"></script>

https://gist.github.com/xiaodaigh/6946423

shiny::runGist("6946423")
